anchor.quote: Here $a$ is the rank of an edge matrix
Let $s$ be the total number of smaller calls over all $W$ roles.

gaps.quote: an edge matrix of rank $a$ costs $a$ smaller calls
gaps.note: The page asserts that an edge matrix of rank a costs exactly a smaller calls but gives no construction or reason showing why the rank sets the number of calls, so the reader cannot check it.

gaps.term: Frame changes cancel along a route
gaps.quote: since frame changes cancel along a route
gaps.note: The page uses cancellation of frame changes along a route as the justification for stating the recursion in vertex frames, but never says what a frame change is or why such changes cancel. The known frame concept does not supply this.

gaps.term: Applicability of the cited bound s < Wm
gaps.quote: The paper proves this in its finite-network section
gaps.note: The cited result s < Wm is stated, but the page does not say why it applies to this recursion's network. It only describes the cited paper's construction (three-element subsets with gather and scatter wires) without relating that construction to the edges and vertices used here.

gaps.quote: so the cost per unit volume is below $m$ times the fixed cost of one call
gaps.note: The step from an average of fewer than m calls per role to a cost per unit volume below m times a fixed cost is not explained. The page never defines the fixed cost of one call or says how cost relates to calls and volume.

gaps.term: Bound on s gives the interchange saving
gaps.quote: The bound on $s$ supplies that saving
gaps.note: The page claims that s < Wm yields a per-volume interchange cost below linear in the field width, but shows no calculation linking the two. It defers to the fast interchange page, which the reader cannot check from this page.
